title: Efficient Discovery of Time Series Motifs under both Length Differences and Warping

problem.claim: Time series motif discovery under Dynamic Time Warping needs to identify similar subsequences that may differ in length.

gap.claim: The existing DTW motif discovery algorithm is confined to fixed-length subsequences.

contributions.claim: A DTW motif discovery approach that handles both length differences and warping.
An algorithm based on the Spikelets time series representation.
A lower bound for DTW in the Spikelet space.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their approach is novel and introduces the first lower bound for DTW in the Spikelet space.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive empirical studies report that the method scales effectively across various real-world datasets.
The studies report that the method efficiently identifies DTW motif pairs of different lengths.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time series motif discovery is important for time series data mining, and DTW is reported to outperform Euclidean Distance in most scenarios.
A prior DTW motif discovery algorithm is limited to fixed-length subsequences.
The work proposes motif discovery under both length differences and warping.
The algorithm uses Spikelets and introduces a lower bound for DTW in Spikelet space.
Empirical studies report scaling across real-world datasets and efficient identification of different-length DTW motif pairs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the algorithmic procedure or computational complexity.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, quantitative results, baselines, or evaluation metrics.
The abstract does not describe the Spikelets representation or the DTW lower-bound derivation.
